research_question: Can Blender-Lab construct and execute coherent optical neural networks from the actual Blender scene with quantitatively valid, reproducible results, useful error certificates and explicit rejection beyond its model?
pilot_scope: Deterministic feasibility of complete scalar path traversal on one fixed represented Blender capture; not confirmatory validation of main H1, field precision, neural accuracy, learning or physical optics.
hypothesis: For this fixed packet and specified ray/depth budgets, the scalar CPU traversal returns COMPLETE with no unresolved or omitted nonzero branches and finite detector estimates.
null_zone: No intermediate values. Supervisor interruption, RAM preflight failure, malformed output or environmental failure are INCONCLUSIVE/NOT_EXECUTED and never silently counted as a geometry result. Algorithmic INCOMPLETE is0.
methodology: Load the byte-pinned captured-scene scalar packet with five explicitly declared unit real source fields. Execute the archived CPU worker once with max-rays4096 and max-depth64 under the stated memory/time profile. Retain raw output and logs before analysis. A valid COMPLETE requires no unresolved rays, all declared source IDs represented, finite complex fields/powers at every declared terminal and no field-certification claim. INCOMPLETE preserves unresolved reasons and null fields. Do not alter geometry, modes, bounds or success criteria after a result; any later profile is a new amendment.
planned_analysis: Deterministic categorical audit and exact path-ledger checks. No p-values, statistical population claim or neural accuracy metric. Record optional timing as supervised pilot duration, not matched-baseline inference cost.
known_limitations: One fixed represented affine scene and one CPU execution; no independent external reproduction.
Exact affine capture model differs from native floating-point transforms and from legacy source JSON descriptors.
Scalar ideal mirrors/splitters/modes do not establish the physical validity of diffraction, polarization or finite-beam coupling.
COMPLETE indicates finite traversal; floating field estimates remain uncertified.
Resource bounds can make traversal incomplete; no post-result increase is allowed in this protocol.
No training, held-out generalization, classifier decision or NVIDIA/AMD result is part of this pilot.
